items.title: MCP parity: bounty_decline + bounty_reject verbs, dispute copy, history order
items.body:
## What

Closes the three door-parity defects QA-MONEY-API proved executed on live production (report: `~/workspace/qawave-2026-10-20/qa-money-api-report.md` in the coordinator's workspace; lane FIX-BOUNTY-MCP-PARITY).

**D-1 — MCP parity verbs.** The hosted full MCP profile exposed 12 `bounty_*` tools but no verb to decline a proposal or reject a submission; both existed only on HTTP, so an MCP-only poster could not complete the money lifecycle. This PR adds:

- `bounty_decline` → dispatches through `escrow.idemExecute` (route `bounty.decline`, status 200) onto `escrow.declineBounty` — the exact transition the HTTP `/decline` route invokes. Poster-only triage of a PROPOSED bounty; the reason is recorded verbatim as `declineReason`.
- `bounty_reject` → `escrow.idemExecute` (route `bounty.reject`, status 200) onto `escrow.rejectWork` — the exact transition the HTTP `/reject` route invokes. Free-miss settlement unchanged: award refunds to the poster in full, worker settles at zero, claim bond forfeited, flake strike recorded, reason in `resolution`.

No parallel ledger logic, no new money semantics, no new error codes: the MCP dispatch pattern (caller derivation, idempotency scoping, EscrowError contract) is the one every existing bounty write tool uses.

**N-1 — `bounty_dispute` copy.** The description promised "dispute a submission", but a pre-verdict submission is not disputable by design (executed refusal `invalid_state`, #3726 Option A). The copy now names the disputable state truthfully: accepted work, inside its challenge window, with the reject/deadline remedies named for submitted work.

**N-2 — `bounty_read_history` ordering.** Documented "newest first" but returned chain/insertion order with lot-less entries (genesis) trailing — non-monotonic in both directions (reproduced locally at base: `n = 7` receipts, genesis last, same-instant pairs in chain order, exactly the QA shape). `escrow.history()` now sorts the read newest-first by recorded time with a chain-position tiebreak. Read-side presentation only: no receipt field changes, the hash chain is untouched, and no consumer depends on the old order (the replay test's receipt set sorts itself; settlement lookup is a find).

## Registrations

- MCP catalog snapshot regenerated in this diff (`scripts/mcp-catalog-snapshot.mjs --write`; re-check clean).
- Canonical hosted tool list (`HOSTED_ROOM_MCP_TOOLS` in `src/room-mcp-join.js`) extended in definition order.
- `KNOWN_UNCOVERED` ratchet in `tests/mcp-tool-contracts.test.js` gains the two tools (the bounty family carries no contract lines by design).
- Catalog count pins, named by hosted CI round 1: `tests/mcp-search-actions.test.js` full-catalog pin 117 → 119; `tests/mcp-untrusted-content.test.js` gains the same explicit accounting it uses for the release tools (each parity verb asserted advertised exactly once on full, never on core, and excluded from the 115-tool existing-catalog budget).
- `docs/BOUNTY-MCP-TOOLS.md`: fourteen tools, both verbs with semantics, dispute line qualified to accepted-only.
- No new server module (the existing MCP tool module is used), no new route rows, no new error codes. The bounty escrow routes are on the legacy hand-rolled chain and carry no route-table parity notes; nothing was dropped.

## Proof

- New `tests/bounty-mcp-parity.test.js` drives the real hosted dispatch against a real RoomStore: MCP-only decline with `declineReason` read back via `bounty_list` as the other member; MCP-only reject with settlement/resolution/balance read-backs and a keyed replay that moves nothing; HTTP decline + reject re-verified unchanged on the same build; `bounty_read_history` asserted monotonic newest-first with genesis last.
- Local gates: the 12 bounty/MCP test files pass (166 tests); `npm run lint` clean; `npm run verify:affected` exit 0 (44 files).
- Bench not owed: no storage, snapshot, sync, or journal write path changes — two dispatch cases onto existing transitions and a read-side sort.

Lands singly (money-adjacent tool surface). The lane never merges; the coordinator posts the LAND-READY record.

items.title: mcp-bounty: contain sync and attachment paths
items.body:
Fixes #27
Fixes #28

`sync_program` used the model-supplied `target_dir` directly and created it. `submit_report` read `poc_files`/`evidence_files` by path and uploaded them to HackerOne. Under prompt injection, either could reach files outside the engagement workspace.

Both paths now resolve through one small helper. The root is `BOUNTY_WORKSPACE_ROOT` (defaults to the server's cwd). It rejects `~`, NUL bytes, paths that resolve outside the root, and symlinks that point out. Absolute paths that stay inside the root still work, so existing workspace paths are unaffected.

I also moved the attachment read before the HackerOne intent is created. A refused path now fails before any network call.

Tests:
- `python -m pytest mcp-bounty-server/tests -q` -> 44 passed, 2 skipped. The skipped cases are the symlink tests on Windows, which need symlink privileges; they should run on macOS/Linux.
- `ruff check` on the changed files passes.

I left the separate installer/scaffold Windows failures out of this change; they're unrelated.

items.title: fix(mcp): report completed bounties as completed and refuse voting on them
items.body:
Fixes #1584 (item 2)

## Problem
Completed bounties that had a voting period retain `isVoting: true` in the database record alongside `inProgress: false`. Because `bountyStatus()` checked `isVoting` before `inProgress`:
1. 379 completed bounties are reported as `status: 'voting'` instead of `'completed'` across MCP and WebMCP tools.
2. `prepareAction` for `vote` and `resolve_vote` only checked `if (!bounty.isVoting)`, allowing transactions to be built for closed bounties which fail on-chain with `NoVotingPeriodSet` (e.g. mainnet 32).
3. `requireOpen()` misreported completed bounties as `voting, not open` instead of `completed, not open`.

## Fix
- In `src/mcp/actions.ts`: in `bountyStatus()`, check `if (!b.inProgress) return 'completed';` before `isVoting`.
- In `prepareAction` for `vote` and `resolve_vote`, guard with `if (!bounty.inProgress || !bounty.isVoting)` so completed bounties reject with `Bounty <id> has no active vote.`.
- Add unit tests covering `bountyStatus` for canceled, completed (with `isVoting: true` and `false`), active voting, and open bounties.
- Add unit tests asserting `prepareAction` rejects `vote` and `resolve_vote` when `inProgress: false` even if `isVoting: true`.

## Verification
- `jest src/mcp` passes 111/111 tests.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` pass with 0 errors.
- Prettier formatted cleanly.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: feat: MCP Tool Runtime — real MCP servers for the Loopfile TOOLS block
items.body:
## Summary

Implements the **MCP Tool Runtime** bounty ($400, listed in `bounties/README.md`): the runtime that makes the Loopfile `TOOLS` block real. Until now `TOOLS` (spec §5b) was schema-only — Loopfiles could declare MCP servers, but nothing resolved, launched, or called them, and the module named `mcp_runtime` was an in-process registry of built-in tools with placeholder browser functions. This PR ships Phase 2 of the MCP roadmap: a stdlib-only MCP client (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio), a runtime that launches each declared server, discovers and namespaces its tools (`server.tool`), routes calls to the owning server, classifies failures the way `docs/mcp-strategy.md` names them (`tool_unavailable` / `tool_timeout` / `tool_error`), and tears servers down at loop exit. `${VAR}` config values are substituted at launch and never logged or traced.

Design, scope, and trace format: [`docs/mcp-runtime.md`](https://github.com/robertomartinezconsultor/infini/blob/feat/mcp-tool-runtime/docs/mcp-runtime.md).

**Honest scope note:** transport is stdio (how local MCP servers run). Local path refs launch directly; GitHub/URL/registry refs resolve when `config.command` says how to launch the server locally, and are otherwise reported `unavailable` with the reason — never silently skipped. A remote HTTP transport and registry resolution are future work, and the doc says so.

## Type

- [x] CLI / Inspector / Observatory
- [ ] Spec change (link to RFC issue)
- [ ] New canonical loop
- [ ] Engine adapter
- [ ] Docs / patterns / essays
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Other

## Spec impact

None. This implements the already-specified §5b `TOOLS` behavior; no files under `spec/` change.

## Conformance

- [x] Add or update an example Loopfile in `examples/` or `loops/` — `examples/mcp-runtime/` (real stdlib MCP server + Loopfile + runnable demo, no LLM key needed)
- [x] Run `infini validate` against every Loopfile in the repo — all pass, including the two new ones
- [x] Added `tests/conformance/mcp-loop/`: `infini conformance tests/conformance` → **9 passed, 0 failed**
- Spec / grammar / schema / compatibility updates: not applicable (no spec change)

## Tests

- [x] This PR adds tests — `cli/tests/test_mcp_runtime.py`: 20 tests. Integration tests spawn a real MCP server subprocess (`cli/tests/mcp_test_server.py`) and speak the actual protocol (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) — no protocol mocks. Coverage: ref parsing, `${VAR}` substitution, namespacing, per-agent filtering, success/error/timeout/unavailable classification, secret hygiene in trace summaries, `Loopfile.tools` parse round-trip, mock-engine trace extension.
- Full suite: `pytest cli/tests` → **51 passed** (31 pre-existing + 20 new).

## Backwards compatibility

Additive only. Loopfiles without a `TOOLS` block behave exactly as before; the built-in tool registry in `mcp_runtime.py` is untouched (the runtime is a new layer in the same module), and the deterministic engine never launches servers, so conformance determinism is preserved.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- [ ] My commits are signed (`git commit -S`) — unsigned; no signing key configured in my environment. Happy to re-sign if required.
- [x] I have used Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `spec:`, `chore:`)
- [x] This PR is one concern (no bundled changes)
- [x] I have updated `CHANGELOG.md` if appropriate

Submitted for the MCP Tool Runtime bounty in `bounties/README.md`. Questions welcome — @nick noted as mentor on the bounty.

items.title: feat: bounty pricing guidance at post time from the room's settled receipts (#3524)
items.body:
Pricing guidance at post time, drawn from the room's own settled receipt history — #3524.

## Derivation (plainly, as filed)
"Comparable work" in #3524 names no taxonomy, so this builds the simplest honest derivation: **the room's own settled receipts, at room level**. A settled receipt is a bounty record in the same room carrying a recorded settlement (`resolution.settlement`, stamped with the immutable `bounty.settled` event) whose worker leg actually paid (`workerMillis > 0`). Guidance = the count of those settled bounties (named in the panel), the min–max range of their settled paid amounts, and the median. Amounts are what workers actually received (net of the 1% room-pool fee on verified-complete payouts; the worker leg on partial dispute splits). Rubric/pinning is summarised from the same settled rows (pinned-rubric criterion counts, approval-mode counts). No similarity engine, no category taxonomy, no cross-room data. Failed/unverified settlements pay 0 and never enter; unsettled bounties have no settlement record and never enter.

## Acceptance mapping
- **Posting flow shows a guidance panel** — web: a panel directly under the post form in `src/bounty-board.js`; agents: the read-only MCP tool `bounty_pricing_guidance`; both read `GET /api/rooms/{roomId}/bounties/pricing-guidance`. Room history example rendered: "Settled bounties in this room paid 9.9–39.6 credits (typical 24.75), from 4 settled bounties in this room… history only, not a recommended price for this bounty." Cold start is a plain sentence ("No settled bounties in this room yet, so there is no pricing history to show.") with **no numbers**.
- **Guidance is read-only; it never blocks posting** — the panel renders no controls; the web panel fetches guidance on its own failure track (`.catch(() => null)`), and tests prove the post form is byte-identical with guidance present, absent, or failing, and that POST /bounties returns 201 before and after settlement data exists.
- **Numbers derived from settled receipts only, labelled as such** — derivation reads only settlement records in the same room; panel/API label them "settled receipts in this room" / historical; a cross-room test proves one room's history never leaks into another room's panel.

## Tests
New `tests/bounty-pricing-guidance.test.js`:
- Pure derivation against a hand-computed fixture (10/20/30/40 credits → range 10–40, median 25; rubric 1–2; modes human 3 / agent 1); odd-count median; cold start carries no numbers; zero-paid settlements excluded.
- Real lifecycles settled through escrow (posted 10/20/30/40 → workers received 9.9/19.8/29.7/39.6 → range 9.9–39.6, median 24.75, count 4); rejected-only and funded-only rooms stay cold; another room stays cold.
- Panel rendering (labels, count named, no controls), panel present/absent/failing form-identity, HTTP cold → settled → posting-unaffected.

items.title: fix(escrow): finalizeBounty pays an approved bounty through the per-bounty door (#3693 residual)
items.body:
## What

The per-bounty finalize door can now pay an `approved` bounty — the residual of #3693 that PR #3865 did not cover.

## Verdict on the residual claim (verified at source on main b9e89d6c8): CONFIRMED

- `_keeperPass` (`server/bounty-escrow.mjs`) has branches for `proposed` / `accepted` / `submitted` / `funded` / `claimed` / `disputed` — **no `approved` branch**. `finalizeBounty` only calls `_keeperPass`, so on an approved bounty it threw `invalid_state`: "bounty is approved: nothing to finalize".
- `closeEpoch` is the only door that paid approved bounties, via its explicit `approved` → `_sweep` intercept. #3865 automated `closeEpoch` (the `escrow-epochs` keeper), so payouts now progress automatically — but the per-bounty door, and with it the MCP `bounty_finalize` tool (`server/mcp-full-profile.mjs` routes to `finalizeBounty`), still could not pay.
- The copy still promises the door pays: `client/bounty-tools.mjs` (`bounty_finalize`): "pay out an approved award past its challenge window"; `docs/BOUNTY-MCP-TOOLS.md`: "payout after the challenge window". Per-bounty door capability before this PR: proposed→expired-unfunded, accepted→approved, submitted→refunded, funded/claimed→refunded, disputed→released/refunded. `approved`→`paid` was missing.

## Fix (shape (a): code made to match the copy)

`finalizeBounty` intercepts the `approved` state exactly as `closeEpoch` does and settles through the **same `_sweep`** — no duplicated settlement code (+14/−1 in `server/bounty-escrow.mjs`). Copy and docs needed no change: they now describe real behaviour.

Semantics preserved:

- **Challenge window:** `_sweep`'s payout/fee moves pass `_requireFinalityMove`, which requires the bounty to sit in `approved` (vested). A bounty can only reach `approved` after its window passed unchallenged (or via a dispute verdict), so nothing can be paid early; finalize on an `accepted` bounty inside its window still throws `invalid_state` (pinned by test).
- **Exactly-once:** the sweep transitions the bounty to `paid`; a second `finalizeBounty` finds nothing to finalize, and a later `closeEpoch` sweeps nothing. Exactly one `payout` journal movement ever exists (asserted, including door/epoch interop).
- **Two-step close:** `closeEpoch` is untouched — its snapshot still keeps a bounty approved by a pass from being swept by that same pass, and the #3865 keeper's tick semantics are unchanged.
- **Conservation:** `verifyConservation` holds throughout; fee (1% to pool), claim-bond return, and the `verified-complete` settlement record all come from `_sweep` itself.

## Tests

New `tests/bounty-finalize-approved.test.js` (3/3):

1. End-to-end through the door only: post → fund → claim → submit → accept → finalize (`approved`, no money moved) → finalize (**`paid`**): worker payable 109.9 (9.9 net of the 1% fee + bond returned), pool 0.1, signed `payout-released` receipt with net/fee/gross exact, exactly one payout journal movement, conservation ok.
2. Exactly-once: after door payment, another finalize throws `invalid_state` and an epoch close sweeps nothing; journal rows and balances unchanged.
3. Differential: the same scenario settled through `finalizeBounty`×2 vs `closeEpoch`×2 yields identical balances for every lane and an identical journal movement shape.

Gates at the fix commit (re-verified at the merged head for the core suites):

- Escrow-related suites: 212/212 pass (bounty-escrow, -epoch-keeper, -finalize-approved, -free-miss, -receipts, -tracks, -atomicity, -http, -release-probes, -anti-flake, -approval-modes, -first-shift-option-b, -journal-replay, -reputation, bounty-tools, mcp-bounty-escrow-errors, public-work-settlement, public-work-settlement-disputes, chaos/escrow-transitions).
- `npm run verify:affected`: exit 0.
- `npm run lint`: exit 0 (0 errors; warnings are the pre-existing baseline, none in the changed lines).

Refs #3693 (the issue's own note leaves closure to the coordinator at deploy verification). Fixers never merge — landing is the coordinator's, at full hosted green at this head.

items.title: C-5 (Ruling 37): posting-time dispute-path warning + honest dispute copy
items.body:
## C-5 (Ruling 37): explicit no-path — posting-time dispute warning + honest dispute copy

Implements candidate C-5 of the DISPUTE-DESIGN pack (Ruling 37 part 1). Today a bounty can be posted with no executable dispute path — no decider named at posting, or a named decider who can never sit — and the poster discovers the dead-end only inside the challenge window, when a dispute refuses `dispute_unavailable`. C-5 moves that information to posting time. It changes **no** designation, seating, or dispute semantics (#3726/#3727 untouched); the warning never blocks posting.

### What changes

- **`server/bounty-escrow.mjs`** — `postBounty` computes the no-path condition over current membership via `_disputePathWarning`: no decider designated (dispute decider, else verifier) → warning that the bounty can never be disputed (designation is posting-time-only); a decider designated but unseatable → run the dispute-time tier-1 resolver (`resolveTier1`, the same code `disputeBounty` seats through, including the human-designee membership card) against every agent member who could do the work, poster as challenger — if no composition seats, warn that as the room stands the bounty cannot be disputed. Result rides the return as `warnings: string[]`.
- **`server/bounty-escrow-routes.mjs`**, **`server/mcp-full-profile.mjs`** — thread `warnings` through both posting doors.
- **`client/bounty-tools.mjs`** — `bounty_dispute` copy fixes nit N-1 (it promised disputing "a submission"; disputes open only on accepted work) and states the decider-named-at-posting condition; `bounty_post` copy states the same and that the response warns when no decider can be seated.
- **`docs/openapi.yaml`** — create-bounty operation documents the dispute-path condition and the `warnings` response field. **`docs/BOUNTY-MCP-TOOLS.md`** — same statements for `bounty_post` / `bounty_dispute`.
- **`tests/bounty-dispute-copy.test.js`** — enumerated 8 specimens: warning fires (no designation, two-member room; verifier is the only other member; human decider with no agent worker; no designation, three-member room), warning silent (verifier named with a worker available; human decider with two agent members), plus two end-to-end truth checks — the warned two-member bounty really refuses its later dispute `dispute_unavailable`, and the unwarned three-member bounty really seats its decider and opens its dispute.

### Verification at head `bdd55807`

- Specimens + named suites at the final head: enumerated 129 tests pass / 0 fail (`bounty-dispute-copy`, `bounty-tools`, `bounty-escrow-routes`, `bounty-escrow`, `bounty-identity`, `mcp-catalog-contract`).

items.title: Cloudflare redirect for mainnet bounty 9 breaks /data and the MCP get_bounty tool
items.body:
A Cloudflare redirect rule sends **every** path under `/mainnet/bounty/9` to `/mainnet/bounty/11`, including the `/data` JSON route. Agents calling `get_bounty` for mainnet #9 get an error instead of data.

**Repro (checked 2026-10-20 03:2xZ):**

```
$ curl -sI https://poidh.xyz/mainnet/bounty/9/data
HTTP/2 301
location: https://poidh.xyz/mainnet/bounty/11      ← /data suffix dropped
server: cloudflare
```

`/mainnet/bounty/11/data` returns JSON (200), but the redirect points at the HTML page, so the MCP gets HTML back:

```
get_bounty { chain: "mainnet", id: 9 }
→ isError: true, "poidh data endpoint returned an invalid response"
```

**Not in the repo:** there's no matching rule in `next.config.js`, `vercel.json` or middleware, and the response comes from `server: cloudflare`. It's a Cloudflare Redirect Rule / Page Rule on the poidh.xyz zone.

**Fix (pick one, in the Cloudflare dashboard → Rules → Redirect Rules):**
1. Keep the rest of the path. Match `http.request.uri.path eq "/mainnet/bounty/9" or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/mainnet/bounty/9/")` (so `/90`, `/91`… aren't caught) and redirect dynamically to `concat("/mainnet/bounty/11", substring(http.request.uri.path, 17))`, so `/9/data` → `/11/data`.
2. Or restrict the rule to the exact page: match `http.request.uri.path eq "/mainnet/bounty/9"` only, so `/9/data` reaches the app.

Option 1 is better: humans and agents both land on #11. Only someone with access to the Cloudflare account can change it.

After the fix, `curl -sI https://poidh.xyz/mainnet/bounty/9/data` should return `location: …/mainnet/bounty/11/data` (or 200).

Found by edge-case reports on bounty Base #1495.
